title: response_schema_mode-resume-token-toolcall-anchoring
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context: Customers are increasingly using structured output via response_format for tightly coupled tool/function calling. We observed two failure modes in production: 1) streaming validation failures mid-stream caused unsafe tool invocations or silent truncation, and 2) opaque errors returned by the OpenAI-compat layer that made automated retries and resume semantics hard for callers. This PR introduces a new explicit response_schema_mode (schema_mode) and a runtime 'resume token' anchoring mechanism that together make mid-stream schema failures actionable and enable safe toolcall fencing and resume flows.

Summary of changes (single-line description): Add response_format.schema_mode with options (strict, soft, resume-friendly), emit structured error payloads with error_code enum, add resume_token generation and validation, add runtime streaming checkpoints (anchoring) to fence tool/function calls when schema violations occur, and extend OpenAI-compat mapping to surface these semantics via function_call compatibility.

Design highlights: 1) response_format.schema_mode - new top-level field in the API: "strict" enforces immediate stream abort on validation failure, "soft" returns best-effort output with schema hints, "resume" produces a structured error (SCHEMA_VIOLATION) containing a resume_token when the generator detects a schema mismatch mid-stream. The resume_token can be sent back with a follow-up request to continue from the last validated checkpoint after prompt corrections or model fallback. 2) error_code enum - standardized codes (SCHEMA_VIOLATION, PARTIAL_OUTPUT, TOOLCALL_FENCED, STREAM_RESUME_HINT) so clients can programmatically handle outcomes. 3) Toolcall fencing - when tool/function call boundaries intersect with validation failures, runtime fences the attempted call, emits TOOLCALL_FENCED and the resume_token, and prevents execution until the resume flow is accepted. 4) OpenAI compatibility - the openai_compat layer now maps the resume_token into function_call metadata when present, and surfaces structured errors as top-level messages compatible with common SDKs.

Implementation notes: Changes touch the streaming validator, the request/response API layer, the OpenAI compatibility mapping, SDK adaptors (Python/TS), the docs page for response_format, and a set of integration tests that exercise race conditions between validation and function calling. The runtime now maintains lightweight per-request checkpoints (anchoring points) every N tokens; these are cryptographic hashes signed by the control plane so resume tokens cannot be forged. Resume flow validates token integrity, the model context that produced it, and enforces that the new prompt includes the user's correction/ack before un-fencing the toolcall.

Backward compatibility and opt-in: Default behavior remains unchanged for requests that do not specify response_format.schema_mode. OpenAI-compat callers get the old best-effort behavior unless they opt into the 'schema_mode' via the compatibility params (see docs).

Testing & rollout: Added unit tests for the validator, 3 integration tests simulating interleaved toolcalls and validation fails, and a non-blocking canary rollout config (10% of traffic) for 72 hours before enabling globally.

Related: Addresses ENG-8342 (streaming schema regressions) and ties to SUP-219 which described a customer incident where a mid-stream validation caused a downstream system to run an unwanted tool.
